Problem: Find all three-digit numbers that are 11 times the sum of their digits.

<reflection>
Let N = 100d_1 + 10d_2 + d_3 with d_1 ∈ {1,...,9}, d_2,d_3 ∈ {0,...,9}. The condition gives 100d_1 + 10d_2 + d_3 = 11(d_1 + d_2 + d_3). Simplification gives 89d_1 - d_2 - 10d_3 = 0, equivalently 89d_1 = d_2 + 10d_3 or d_2 = 89d_1 - 10d_3. For d_1 = 1, d_2 = 89 - 10d_3 and the digit constraint is 0 ≤ 89 - 10d_3 ≤ 9. Testing d_3 = 0, 1, 2 gives invalid d_2 values 89, 79, 69.
This conclusion is false because the search was not completed; for d_1 = 1, d_3 = 8 gives d_2 = 9, producing the valid number 198.
Continue checking all remaining digit values d_3 = 3,...,9 under the constraint 0 ≤ 89 - 10d_3 ≤ 9, then verify any candidate number.
</reflection>
